title: Company Answers: a cited Q&A page on your own content
description: The hello-world of Glean apps: one page, one input, one permission-aware cited answer, built two ways, with the Web SDK and with the Chat API.

preview.caption: A permission-aware answer grounded in company knowledge.

steps.title: Copy the project onto your machine
steps.description: Creates a company-answers folder in whatever directory you run this from. Every command after this one runs inside that folder.

steps.title: Install dependencies
steps.description: Installs the Glean Web SDK and the Vite dev server that hosts the page.

steps.title: Find your Glean tenant
steps.description: Your email is used once to find which Glean tenant you belong to. The command creates .env.local and fills in VITE_GLEAN_BACKEND. It does not set the first question.

steps.title: Set the first question
steps.description: Open .env.local and set VITE_GLEAN_INITIAL_MESSAGE to a question about content you know exists in Glean, for example your PTO policy. The page seeds chat with that question.

steps.title: Open the page
steps.description: Starts Vite and prints a Local URL. Open that URL yourself in your normal browser where you are already signed in to Glean.

steps.title: Check it against your own content
steps.description: Once the page is open in your signed-in browser, confirm Glean's chat UI renders a cited answer to the question you set. Try a second topic you know exists.

questions.prompt: What is your work email? It is used once to discover your Glean tenant.
What topic do you know exists in your Glean content?

run.url: the Local URL printed by the server

steps.title: Copy the project onto your machine
steps.description: Creates a company-answers folder in whatever directory you run this from. Every command after this one runs inside that folder.

steps.title: Install dependencies
steps.description: Installs the Glean API client and the small local server that serves the page.

steps.title: See it work before you connect anything
steps.description: Runs the page against recorded answers for a fictional company named Acme, so you can see cited PTO answers before you connect anything. This needs no Glean credentials.

steps.title: Sign in to Glean
steps.description: Your email is used once to find which Glean tenant you belong to, then a browser window opens for you to approve access. The command creates the .env file for you and fills in GLEAN_SERVER_URL and GLEAN_API_TOKEN. If your tenant has not enabled OAuth, skip this command and do it by hand instead: copy .env.example to .env, then fill in your Glean instance URL and a Glean API token that has the CHAT scope.

steps.title: Choose a question you know your docs can answer
steps.description: Signing in does not pick a topic for you, so open .env and set GLEAN_DEMO_QUERY to a question about your own content, for example your PTO policy.

steps.title: Check it against your own content
steps.description: Takes 1 to 3 minutes. It starts its own server, asks your Glean instance the question you set, and fails if the answer comes back without citing a real document.

steps.title: Open the page
steps.description: Starts the server and prints a Local URL. Open that URL in your browser.

steps.title: Pick a path
steps.description: Path A (Web SDK) renders Glean's own chat UI for you. Fastest to stand up, no backend code. Path B (Chat API) calls glean.chat.create from your own backend. You own every pixel of the UI. Both end in the same place: a permission-aware, cited answer.

aiPrompt: Build Company Answers following https://developers.glean.com/cookbook/company-answers. Ask whether to use (A) Web SDK or (B) Chat API, then collect that path's inputs before starting. Path A: run the shipped configure command with the work email already supplied, write VITE_GLEAN_BACKEND, then set VITE_GLEAN_INITIAL_MESSAGE to the topic they know exists. Start Vite, report the exact local URL, and wait for the user to open it in their normal signed-in browser. Never automate that browser. Path B: run npm run verify:fixture first (no credentials). Sign in with the shipped login command, which writes GLEAN_SERVER_URL and GLEAN_API_TOKEN only. Then set GLEAN_DEMO_QUERY to their topic. Keep the token server-side. Call the Chat API with glean.chat.create, stream:false, store:false, and X_GLEAN_INCLUDE_EXPERIMENTAL=true. Parse ASSISTANT OUTPUT_TEXT content and citations from annotations[].sources. Retry empty output once. Verify a cited answer on the user's own content before claiming live success.
llmContext: Path A uses renderChat with an explicit backend and the user's existing Glean browser session; live verification is user-mediated in their normal signed-in browser. Path B uses the Chat API through glean.chat.create with stream:false, store:false, and X_GLEAN_INCLUDE_EXPERIMENTAL=true. Construct Glean with apiToken plus serverURL. Read ASSISTANT OUTPUT_TEXT content and citations from annotations[].sources. Retry empty output once. Default first run is npm run verify:fixture with GLEAN_USE_FIXTURE=true. Login does not write GLEAN_DEMO_QUERY.

content.problem:
Every team has the same first Glean app: a single page where anyone can ask
a company question and get a cited, permission-aware answer. There are two
equally valid ways to build it — this recipe builds both, side by side, so
you can pick the trade-off that fits your app.
takeItFurther: Swap in a specific agent by passing its `agentId` to `renderChat` on Path A.
Keep Path B on `stream:false` until you own a stream parser for Chat API events.
